Yet sinful human beings can be so dissatisfied that nothing God gives them seems enough.
The Lord does good to all humanity, while showing his people special care.
Many believers have come close to falling into sin or despair.
God has shown his goodness by preventing their fall or quickly restoring them through grace and comfort.
Everyone carrying the heavy burden of sin may come to Christ in faith.
He will relieve and raise them.
The Lord willingly hears and answers his people's prayers.
He is present everywhere, yet in a special way near to those who call upon him sincerely.
By faith he lives within their hearts, and they remain in him.
He comes near in every hour of need, so that those who call upon him in truth and sincerity may receive what they ask and find what they seek.
He has taught them to love his name and holy ways.
He will therefore deliver them from the destruction awaiting the unrepentant.
May we love his name, obey his ways and pray that all humanity will praise his holy name forever.

row.cell: Why we should not trust in men.
Why we should trust in God.

div.title: Human help is short-lived (verses 1–4)
div.p: Those who delight in praising God now will praise him forever. What little value worldly pursuits have compared with that prospect!

There is one Son of Man in whom help never fails, who is also the Son of God. All other sons of men share fallen Adam's condition. Adam did not remain in his original honor; neither can any other human being guarantee lasting happiness.

God gave the earth to humanity, yet people constantly struggle over it. Eventually even the most powerful person owns nothing but the small piece of ground where the body is buried. On the day of death, all earthly plans perish. We should not make other people the ultimate ground of our hope.

div.title: The Lord's eternal help and kingdom (verses 5–10)
div.p: For this life we hope in God's providence, and for the next we hope in his grace.
The God of heaven became human in order to save us. He died upon the cross for our sins and was laid in the grave; nevertheless, his purposes of love did not end there. He rose again to fulfill them.

Christ's earthly miracles picture the saving works he continues to perform every day. He liberates prisoners from sin and Satan, opens the eyes of understanding, feeds people who hunger for salvation with the bread of life, and shows mercy to the poor in spirit, the helpless and the spiritually fatherless.
His kingdom continues forever. Let sinners turn to him and believers rejoice in him. Let us encourage one another to praise his name.

row.cell: The people of God are exhorted to praise him for his mercies and care.
For the salvation and prosperity of the church.

div.title: God gathers, heals and provides (verses 1–11)
div.p: Praising God is work that carries its own reward. It is fitting for all rational creatures and especially for people bound to him by covenant.

He gathers outcast sinners through grace and brings them into his holy dwelling. Through the comfort of his Spirit, he heals the brokenhearted, speaks peace and assures them that their sins are pardoned.

Our knowledge quickly reaches its limits, but God's wisdom cannot be measured. He counts the stars and listens to the brokenhearted. He feeds young ravens; surely he will not neglect his praying people.
Clouds appear dark, yet without them there would be no rain or fruit. Likewise clouds of affliction can yield the peaceful fruit of righteousness.

God does not admire the outward powers and achievements in which sinners glory. He values sincere reverence and trust. Faithful people should act under the gracious influence of hope and fear joined together.

div.title: God's word and Spirit melt frozen hearts (verses 12–20)
div.p: God's wisdom, power and goodness build and preserve his church as they preserved Jerusalem. His blessings in nature picture his gracious work.
The word that makes winter ice melt can represent the gospel of Christ, while the thawing wind pictures the Spirit of Christ, whom Scripture compares to the wind (John 3:8).

Converting grace softens a heart that was frozen hard, melting it into tears of repentance and releasing good thoughts and affections once held back. The change brought about by the thaw is visible although its workings are mysterious. So is the transformation when God's word and Spirit bring a soul to repentance and life.

row.cell: The creatures placed in the upper world called on to praise the Lord.
Also the creatures of this lower world, especially his own people.

div.title: The heavens praise their Creator (verses 1–6)
div.p: We know little of the heavenly world of light while living in this dark and sinful world. Yet we know that holy angels dwell there and continually praise God.
The psalmist calls them to praise him in the finest possible way. By joining them we acknowledge our fellowship with the spirits above.
The heavens and everything within them declare the Lord's glory. They call us to honor the Creator and Redeemer of the universe in both words and deeds.

div.title: Every creature and every person called to praise (verses 7–14)
div.p: God is praised even in a fallen world. Nature's strongest and stormiest forces do only what he directs. People who rebel against his word may seem more violent than storm winds, but they cannot thwart his purpose.
Mountains and hills, barren and fertile alike, give reasons for praise. Rational creatures should praise him especially, whatever their social position.
His saints should praise him continually. He is not only our Creator but our Redeemer, who has brought his people near.

Henry says that “the horn of his people” may mean Christ, whom God has exalted as Prince and Savior, the eternal defense and praise of his saints. Redemption displays extraordinary glory and supplies the foundation for our hope and joy.
May the Lord forgive us and teach us to love him more and praise him better.

row.cell: Joy to all the people of God.

div.title: A new song for the new creation (verses 1–5)
div.p: New mercies call for new songs of praise, on earth and in heaven.
The children of Zion should thank God for creating them, but also for making them new creations in Christ Jesus for good works. They were not merely made human; he formed them as saints.
The Lord takes pleasure in his people; they should delight in him.
When sinners feel their need and unworthiness, God clothes them with the graces of his Spirit and restores his image within them. Their joy will continue forever.
Let believers sing even during wakeful nights. On their deathbeds, they can rejoice in the hope of eternal rest and glory.

div.title: Christ's victory is not spread by human violence (verses 6–9)
div.p: Certain servants of God in ancient times were specifically appointed to carry out his judgments, not from private revenge or political ambition, but in obedience to a particular command.
But the victory promised to all God's saints concerns the enemies of their salvation.

p.hi: Christ did not intend his gospel to be spread by fire and sword, nor his righteousness by human wrath.

div.p: Instead, let his praises be in our mouths and the sword of the word of God in our hands, with the shield of faith as we struggle against the world, the flesh and the devil.
Through the blood of the Lamb and his testimony, believers will become more than conquerors. Final judgment will be carried out on the great day.
Henry also asks us to picture Christ and his gospel church, especially in what he calls her millennial condition.

Christ and his people rejoice in one another. Through their prayers and efforts, they work with him as he advances in the chariots of salvation, conquering sinners by grace, or in chariots of vengeance, bringing destruction upon his enemies.

p.hi: A psalm of praise.

div.title: Everything that breathes, praise the Lord
div.p: We are summoned to praise God in his sanctuary and for the privilege of worshiping him.
The heavens display his power and glory in ways that their blessed inhabitants see far more fully than we do.
Yet his greatest mighty work has been revealed in his earthly sanctuary: the redemption of human beings.
God's holiness and love shine more clearly in redemption than in all his other works.
We should therefore praise our God and Savior.
The precise names of the musical instruments are not the heart of the passage. What matters is that we spare no effort or expense in serving God.
Praise him with strong faith.
Praise him through holy love and delight.
Praise him with complete confidence in Christ.
Praise him in believing triumph over the powers of darkness.
Praise him through obedience to every command.
Praise him with cheerful submission to all his appointments.
Praise him by rejoicing in his love and taking comfort in his goodness.
Praise him by promoting the interests of the kingdom of grace.
Praise him with hope in the kingdom of his glory.
Soon each of us will draw a final breath. Therefore, while we still have breath, let us praise the Lord, so that even death may find us full of comfort.
Let everything that breathes praise the Lord. Praise the Lord!
This is a fitting conclusion to the book of Psalms, inspired by the Spirit and written for praise.
Henry emphasizes that it has provided songs for God's people for more than three thousand years, and he calls it the book most frequently quoted by Christ and his apostles.
It speaks of God's majesty and government, addresses every human condition and every sort of spiritual experience, and displays clear marks of divine inspiration.

div.title: Proverbs — Separate book introduction (Modern English candidate)
div.p: Henry explains the purpose of Proverbs by expanding the opening verses of the book.
First, these are the proverbs of Solomon, David's son and king of Israel.
Second, they concern knowledge of wisdom, devotion toward God, moral instruction and discipline, and understanding counsel that is wise and prudent.
Third, they teach how to acquire practical wisdom. True wisdom becomes visible in the way a person lives, especially in righteous conduct toward other human beings.

Fourth, they give simple people discernment through sound principles and a correct understanding of good and evil. They give the young knowledge so they need not go wrong through ignorance, and discretion through considering God's commands so they need not go wrong through stubbornness.
Henry contrasts this teaching with proverbs from other nations, many of which he says are grounded in selfishness, cunning, pride, injustice, national contempt and hostility.
Solomon's proverbs instead rest upon godliness, charity, justice, benevolence and genuine prudence.
Their complete moral purity, Henry concludes, shows that they are the word of God.

row.cell: Exhortations to fear God and obey parents.
To avoid the enticings of sinners.
The address of Wisdom to sinners.

div.title: Why these proverbs teach us (verses 1–6)
div.p: The lessons in Proverbs are straightforward and will greatly benefit people who recognize how little they know and how much they need to be taught.
Young people who govern their lives by these instructions will grow in both understanding and discretion.
Solomon teaches the most important truths. But one greater than Solomon speaks here.
Christ speaks through his word and Spirit.
He is the Word and the Wisdom of God, and he himself has become wisdom for us.

div.title: Reverence for God and instruction from parents (verses 7–9)
div.p: Fools are people who possess no real wisdom and follow whatever schemes they invent, disregarding both reason and reverence for God.
Children are rational creatures.
When we explain what they should do, we ought also to explain why.
Yet children are fallen and often stubborn, so instruction must be accompanied by rules and authority.
Let us consider God's truths and commandments worthy of the highest honor.
If we truly treasure them, their excellence will be evident in our lives.

div.title: Refusing to follow sinners (verses 10–19)
div.p: Wicked people eagerly invite others onto paths leading to destruction.
Sinners like company in their sins, and for that reason their responsibility becomes even greater.
Young people should be exceedingly careful.

p.hi: Do not consent.

div.p: Do not speak as they speak, act as they act or do what they want you to do.
Do not share in their wrongdoing.
How terrible that someone could enjoy another person's destruction!
They prize worldly wealth as though it were something truly substantial or precious.
But many thousands have ruined themselves by valuing the world's riches too highly.
Sinners imagine that wrongdoing will benefit them.
The path of sin, however, runs downhill and soon escapes their control.
Those who want to avoid destruction in this life and the next must refuse even the first step onto that path.
Greed drives people into practices that shorten their lives and harm others.
What would a person gain by acquiring the entire world while losing life—and how much worse to lose the soul?

div.title: Wisdom calls sinners to repentance (verses 20–33)
div.p: Solomon has shown the danger of listening to Satan's temptations.
He now shows how dangerous it is to refuse God's invitation.
Christ himself is Wisdom.
He addresses three groups.
First, the simple: people content with shallow ideas of good and evil, prejudiced against the Lord's ways, who flatter themselves about their sins.
Second, mockers: proud people who laugh at everything holy and turn sincere religion into a joke.
Third, fools: those who positively hate being instructed and have become deeply hostile to godliness.
The command is plain: Turn when Wisdom rebukes you.
We have not responded rightly to rebuke unless we turn from evil to good.
God gives extraordinary encouragement.
No one can accomplish sincere conversion through personal strength, but he promises: I will pour out my Spirit to you.
Conversion requires special grace, and that grace will not be refused to those who seek it.
Christ's love and promises should make us listen carefully even when he rebukes us.
How long do sinners expect to remain safe on such a dangerous path, knowing how uncertain life is and what it means to die without Christ?
They may now feel secure and dismiss every warning.
But calamity will come.
Now God offers to hear their prayers; those who persist in rejecting him may later cry out too late.
Are we still despising Wisdom?
Let us listen diligently and obey the Lord Jesus, finding peace of conscience, confidence in God and deliverance from evil in life, death and eternity.

row.cell: Promises to those who seek wisdom.

div.title: Seeking the wisdom God freely gives (verses 1–9)
div.p: Those who earnestly seek wisdom from heaven will never regret the effort they have made.
The gift is free, but that does not remove the need for diligence in seeking it (John 6:27).
Those who seek will find; those who ask will receive.
Who receives this blessing?
The righteous, upon whom God's image is renewed, an image that includes true righteousness.
When we depend upon God and seek wisdom from him, he will enable us to walk in the paths of justice.

div.title: Wisdom protects the heart and conduct (verses 10–22)
div.p: Those who are truly wise avoid evil company and evil practices.
When wisdom governs us, it does not merely fill the mind with information.
It enters the heart.
It protects against both the corruption already within us and temptation arriving from outside.
Sin's ways are dark, unsafe and joyless.
How foolish to leave the bright and peaceful paths of uprightness for such roads!
Some people delight in both committing sin and watching others sin.
A wise person avoids their company.
He also avoids people who encourage lustful actions that defile the body, the living temple, and fight against the soul.
These are dangers that distress godly people and give thoughtful parents reason to be concerned for their children.
The suffering of others should serve as a warning.
Our Lord Jesus warned against sinful pleasures by speaking of the everlasting torments that follow them.
People caught in these traps rarely free themselves easily.
Sin's deceit hardens the heart and blinds the understanding.
Henry notes that many readers also understand these warnings figuratively, applying them to idolatry or to making the soul a servant of the body by pursuing forbidden objects.
The righteous and wicked alike will eventually leave this earth.
But the earth serves very different purposes for them.
For an unrepentant sinner, it is all the heaven that person will ever possess.
For the righteous, it is a place to prepare for heaven.
Does it not matter to us whether we share the wicked person's end or the everlasting joys promised to believers?

row.cell: To piety, and to improve afflictions.

div.title: Trust the Lord rather than your own understanding (verses 1–6)
div.p: The life of believing obedience generally brings peace and health.
Even if it does not lengthen our earthly days, we will live forever in heaven.
Hold tightly to mercy and truth: God's mercy in making promises and his faithfulness in keeping them.
Walk consistently with both, treasure them and receive their comfort.
Trust in the Lord with your whole heart, believing that he is willing, wise and able to do what is best.
Those who know themselves find their own understanding a broken reed that cannot bear their weight.
Do not make plans that violate God's law.
Ask him to direct you even when a decision seems obvious.
In pleasant and successful circumstances, acknowledge him with thanks.
When a road is difficult and hedged in by thorns, acknowledge him with submission.
God will direct your paths, making them safe and ultimately good.

div.title: Honoring God and learning from fatherly correction (verses 7–12)
div.p: Few things are more destructive to reverence for God than conceit about our own wisdom.
The prudence and moderation religion teaches benefit both soul and body.
Earthly wealth is poor and perishable, but even that should be used to honor God.
Those who do good with what they have can be entrusted with more opportunities to do good.
When the Lord sends sickness and hardship, remember that he addresses us as his children.
Do not lose courage under a prolonged trial, surrender to despair or use sinful methods to seek relief.
A loving father corrects a child because he loves the child and wants that child to become wise and good.
Through grace, affliction may actually increase the holiness of God's people.

div.title: Wisdom more valuable than treasure (verses 13–20)
div.p: No jewel or earthly treasure compares with true wisdom, whether we consider this life or eternity.
Make obtaining wisdom your serious pursuit, willing to give up everything for it.
This Wisdom is Jesus Christ and the salvation he gives, received through faith and prayer.
Our unbelief, remaining sin and carelessness often lead us away from his pleasant paths, causing our own sorrow.
Christ is the Wisdom through whom the worlds were created and by whom they continue to exist.
Happy are those to whom God has made him their wisdom.
He possesses everything needed to fulfill his promises.

div.title: Wisdom guards our steps (verses 21–26)
div.p: Do not let Christ's words slip away from your attention.
Keep sound wisdom and discretion.
When we follow the Lord, his providence guards our natural life and his grace preserves our spiritual life.
He can keep us from falling into sin or being crushed by trouble.

div.title: Acting justly and avoiding unnecessary conflict (verses 27–35)
div.p: Our duty is to obey Christ's commands and follow his example.
Act justly, love mercy and beware of greed.
Be ready for every good work.
Avoid quarrels that serve no purpose.
When possible, it is better to bear a wrong patiently than to engage in pointless legal disputes.
Little lasting good comes from needless fighting.
Do not envy oppressive people who enjoy prosperity.
A disciple of Christ should not imitate their methods.
Greedy and self-indulgent people may mock such teaching, but their portion is everlasting contempt.
God favors the humble believer.

row.cell: Exhortation to the study of wisdom.
Cautions against bad company, Exhortation to faith and holiness.

div.title: Receiving the instruction of wisdom (verses 1–13)
div.p: We should regard faithful teachers as fathers and welcome their instruction, even when it includes correction and rebuke.
Solomon's parents instructed him because they loved him.
Wise and godly people in every age and social position agree that true wisdom is expressed through obedience and joined to real happiness.
Seek that wisdom diligently.
Especially seek mastery over the sinful desires within your own heart.
Work harder to obtain this spiritual wisdom than to acquire worldly riches.
Nothing is more necessary than a saving share in Christ.
A soul without wisdom and grace is spiritually dead.
How pitiful to possess wealth, status and power but die without understanding, without Christ, without hope and without God!
Listen to the One who has the words of eternal life.
Hold firmly to his instruction.
Then your path will be clear, and you can avoid being trapped or stumbling.

div.title: Avoiding evil paths and guarding the heart (verses 14–27)
div.p: The path of wicked people can appear pleasant or like the quickest way to accomplish something.
But it is evil and will end in harm.
If you love God and care for your soul, stay far away.
Do not simply try to keep an adequate distance from temptation.
Go as far from it as you can.
The path of the righteous is light, for Christ is both their Way and their Light.
They will not become perfectly holy until heaven, but there they will shine like the sun.
The path of sin is darkness.
Wicked people stumble without knowing why, and often do not reflect on why God has brought hardship upon them or what the outcome may be.
Listening attentively to Scripture is evidence that grace has begun working in the heart and a means through which that work grows.
God's word contains the right remedy for every disease of the soul.
Guard your heart with all diligence.
Protect it from doing harm and being harmed, because life flows from the heart.
Above all, ask the Lord Jesus for living water—the Holy Spirit who sanctifies and gives life that lasts forever.
Then you can put away corrupt speech and dishonest lips.
Turn your eyes away from empty attractions and look straight ahead.
Follow the rule of God's word and walk in the footsteps of the Lord and Master.
Lord, forgive our past sins and help us follow you more faithfully in the future.

row.cell: Exhortations to wisdom. The evils of licentiousness.
Remedies against licentiousness, The miserable end of the wicked.

div.title: Keep far from sexual temptation (verses 1–14)
div.p: Solomon warns young men, whom he addresses as his children, to refuse lustful desires.

Some readers understand the adulterous woman as a picture of idolatry or false doctrine, because both corrupt beliefs and conduct. But the passage's direct subject is sin against the seventh commandment.
Sexual wrongdoing has also repeatedly become a means by which Satan draws people from the worship of God into false religion.
Consider its terrible consequences. Sin's fruit is bitter, whichever aspect we consider. It wounds the person who follows it and leads to the torments of hell.
Its natural tendency is to destroy both body and soul.
We should therefore avoid not only the act itself but also everything that might lead to it.
Those who wish to avoid harm should keep away from danger.
If we deliberately put ourselves into temptation and then pray, Lead us not into temptation, we mock God.
Such sin damages reputation, wastes time, consumes property, destroys health and fills the mind with horror.
A person may feel merry now, but sooner or later sorrow will follow.
Someone convinced of sin's guilt blames personal folly rather than inventing excuses.
Repeated acts of sin become entrenched habits.
Through an extraordinary act of divine mercy, true repentance can prevent the final ruin of such a sinner.
But Henry warns that this is uncommon; many people die as they have lived.
What words could express the misery of a person who has destroyed himself and enters eternity tormented by an accusing conscience?

div.title: God's provision of marriage and his knowledge of all our ways (verses 15–23)
div.p: Lawful marriage is a God-appointed means of avoiding destructive sexual sins.
Yet marriage is not lived rightly unless the spouses attend to God's word, seek his direction and blessing, and act with genuine affection toward one another.
Always remember that hidden sins may escape human notice, but our ways are before the Lord.
He not only sees our conduct; he examines every step.
Those who foolishly choose a path of sin may justly be left by God to follow their own choices until those choices bring destruction.

row.cell: Exhortations to walk according to God's commandments.

div.title: Beware of careless financial guarantees (verses 1–5)
div.p: Living according to God's word benefits us even in the present life.
We are stewards, not absolute owners, of our possessions. We will answer to the Lord for how we use them.
It is wrong to waste them through rash projects or agreements that may entangle us in difficulty and temptations.
No one should promise to pay another person's debt unless the amount is something they are able and willing to pay, without depriving their own family of what it needs.
When we guarantee a debt, we should consider it our own obligation.
If such care is necessary to escape debts owed to other people, how much more earnestly should we seek release from our debt before God!
Humble yourself before him. Seek Christ as your Friend and Advocate, and pray earnestly for forgiveness of sin and deliverance from destruction.

div.title: Learn diligence from the ant (verses 6–11)
div.p: Diligence in our work is both wise and right.
Its main purpose is not simply to become wealthy, but to avoid burdening others or bringing disgrace upon God's church.
Ants show more industry than lazy people. We can learn from even the smallest creatures and be ashamed by their example.
Habits of idleness and excessive self-indulgence grow stronger through repetition.
A wasted life leads toward poverty. At first poverty seems distant, like a traveler slowly approaching. When it arrives, it becomes like an armed man whom the careless person cannot resist.
The same warning applies to the soul.
How many people delight in the sleep of sin and dream of worldly happiness!
We should seek to wake them. We must also be diligent concerning our own salvation.

div.title: Turn away from the things God hates (verses 12–19)
div.p: If people who do nothing useful deserve rebuke, those who devote themselves to doing as much evil as possible deserve still stronger condemnation.
The wicked person described here plans speech and conduct cunningly and deliberately.
Destruction can overtake such a person suddenly and without remedy.
The passage lists seven things God hates.
Sins that destroy the peace and well-being of other people are particularly offensive to him.
We must learn to hate these sins in ourselves. Merely condemning them in other people accomplishes nothing.
Avoid such conduct; remain watchful and pray against it.
Show clear disapproval of those who practice it, whatever their rank or position.

div.title: Walk in God's commandments (verses 20–35)
div.p: God's word has something to teach us in every circumstance of life.
We should never resent faithful correction.
The repeated warnings against adultery are necessary because the sin is widespread and deeply evil.
Its consequences are destructive, and it can ruin the soul's spiritual life.
Notice how this chapter brings together its warnings.
Remember the One who willingly became our Surety—Christ—while we were strangers and enemies.
With such promises, motives and an example before us, how could Christians remain idle or careless?
Will we neglect the things pleasing to God and worthy of the gracious reward he promises?
We must guard every sense through which sinful influence can enter our thoughts and affections.

row.cell: The arts of seducers, with warnings against them.

div.title: Keep God's commands close to your heart (verses 1–5)
div.p: We must treasure God's commands and guard them carefully.
The instruction is more than “Keep them, and you will live.” We should keep them as people who cannot live without them.
Some people dismiss careful, conscientious obedience as unnecessarily strict.
But God's law is to be guarded like the pupil of the eye.
Indeed, when God's law is written on the heart, it serves as the eye of the soul.
Let the word of God dwell within us and be written where it will always be available for us to read and recall.
In this way we are protected against the destructive effects of our sinful desires and the traps of Satan.
Let God's word strengthen both our fear of sin and our determination to avoid it.

div.title: Beware the ways of seducers (verses 6–27)
div.p: This passage gives a deeply moving example of the danger of youthful lust.
Whether understood as history or as a parable, it teaches a vital lesson.
After such a vivid account of the danger of approaching sexual temptation, who would dare to place themselves deliberately in its path?
That would resemble a person dancing at the edge of a high cliff immediately after watching someone else fall over it.
Those who bring ruin upon themselves begin by disregarding God's good commands.
We should pray every day that God will keep us from running into temptation.
Otherwise, we virtually invite the enemies of our souls to lay traps for us.
Keep well away from places and situations that encourage vice.
Beware especially of sins advertised as pleasant.
Their apparent attractiveness makes them more dangerous: they readily capture the heart and harden it against repentance.
Consider how an action will end before you begin it.
Even if someone lived as long as Methuselah and spent every day enjoying the greatest pleasures sin could offer, one hour of the anguish and trouble following such a life would outweigh them all.

row.cell: Christ, as Wisdom, calls to the sons of men.
The nature and riches of Wisdom.
Christ one with the Father, in the creation of the world, and rejoicing in his work for the salvation of man.

div.title: Christ, God's Wisdom, calls to humanity (verses 1–11)
div.p: God makes his will known through creation and human conscience, but more clearly through Moses and the prophets.
The main difficulty is persuading people to pay attention to the instruction they receive.
Yet when even the most ignorant person listens to Christ's words, that teaching can lead to a saving knowledge of the truth.
Where a person has an understanding heart and willingly receives truth with love, wisdom becomes more precious than silver or gold.

div.title: The character and riches of Wisdom (verses 12–21)
div.p: Here Wisdom is Christ, in whom are hidden all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge.
He is Christ in the word and Christ in the heart: not only Christ revealed to us, but Christ revealed within us.
Every form of true prudence and ability comes from the Lord.
Through the redemption purchased by Christ's precious blood, the riches of grace overflow in wisdom and good judgment.
Human beings have invented many ways to destroy themselves. God has provided one way to restore us.
Christ hates pride, arrogance, evil conduct and dishonest speech.
These sins make people resistant to his humbling, awakening and holy instruction.
True religion offers the soundest counsel when we face difficult decisions, and helps us see our path clearly.
Christ's wisdom makes those who receive it through love for him genuinely happy.
Seek him early, earnestly and before everything else. Christ has never told anyone to seek him in vain.
People who love him have seen his loveliness and have experienced his love poured into their hearts.
They are blessed here, or in the incomparably better life to come.
Wealth obtained through vanity soon diminishes.
But possessions gained honestly can be put to good use, and what is rightly spent upon godliness and charity has a lasting benefit.
If God's people lack riches and honor in the present world, he will give them something infinitely better.
They enjoy his grace even now.
Through his Spirit, Christ guides them into truth and righteousness; they walk according to the Spirit.
They will also enjoy God's glory hereafter.
Wisdom's promises store up blessings not merely for days or years but for eternity.
That is why her fruit is better than gold.

div.title: The eternal Son and the creation of the world (verses 22–31)
div.p: In Henry's exposition, the Son of God declares that he was involved in creating the world.
How perfectly suited the Creator of the world is to be its Savior!
Before the world began, the Son was appointed to that great saving work.
If he delights in saving miserable sinners, how could we fail to delight in his salvation?

div.title: Hear Christ's voice (verses 32–36)
div.p: We should listen to Christ with the readiness of obedient children.
Let us not refuse such mercy.
Blessed are those who hear the Savior's voice and wait upon him through daily Scripture reading, meditation and prayer.
People devoted to the world make time for empty amusements while still attending to what they regard as essential.
When professing believers seek excuses to neglect the means of grace, do they not show contempt for Wisdom's instruction?
Christ is both Wisdom and Life to everyone who believes.
We cannot obtain God's favor unless we find Christ and are found in him.
Those who offend Christ injure their own souls.
Sinners are destroyed because they choose the way of destruction.
God therefore remains just when he judges them.

div.title: Wisdom invites people to Christ (verses 1–12)
div.p: Christ has prepared ordinances through which those who believe receive spiritual nourishment in this life, and dwelling places in heaven where they will be received afterward.
Ministers of the gospel go out to invite guests to this feast.
The invitation is open to everyone; it excludes no one except those who refuse to come.
Our Savior came not to call people who consider themselves righteous, but sinners.
He did not come to call those who are wise in their own eyes and think they already see clearly.
We must leave the companionship and foolish pleasures of ungodly people if we are to enjoy the pleasures of a holy life.
Seeking out the company of wicked people in the confident expectation of doing them good is dangerous: we are often more likely to be corrupted by them.
It is not enough to abandon the foolish; we must join those who walk in wisdom.
True wisdom is found in the way of godliness, and true life lies at the end of that way.
Those who embrace it are blessed.
We cannot add anything to God's own happiness or profit him through our obedience. The benefit is ours, not his.
But consider the disgrace and destruction awaiting those who disregard Wisdom's invitation.
God is not the author of sin.
Satan can tempt, but he cannot force anyone to sin.
Those who scorn this offer must bear the loss of what they have rejected. Their contempt makes their condemnation greater.

div.title: Folly offers a deceptive invitation (verses 13–18)
div.p: See how diligently the tempter works to draw unwary people into sin.
Worldly and sensual pleasures dull the conscience and extinguish the first sparks of conviction.
Folly cannot offer sound reasons for following her.
When she rules a person's soul, knowledge of holy things is forgotten and lost.
Her invitations are persistent and demanding.
We need to seek true wisdom and pray for it, because Satan has many ways of drawing our souls away from Christ.
Not only bodily lusts and openly wicked seducers endanger people.
False teachers also lead thousands toward destruction with doctrines that flatter pride and grant permission to sinful desire.
They are especially dangerous to people whose first serious concern for their souls has not yet taken deep root.
Satan's depths are the depths of hell.
Unrepented sin ends in destruction without remedy.
Solomon shows us the hook hidden beneath the bait. Those who believe his warning will not reach for it.
Notice how miserable, empty, unsatisfying and deceptive are the pleasures sin offers, even when they seem to have been stolen for our enjoyment.
May our desire for the eternal enjoyment of Jesus Christ become so strong that we live by faith for him each day now and soon live with him in glory.

div.title: Original chapter-level introductory comment
div.p: Throughout Proverbs, we should look for a meaning beyond each passage's first and most immediate application. Henry sees that deeper meaning in Jesus Christ, the Wisdom so often spoken of throughout this book.

div.title: Verse 1 — Children and their parents
div.p: Parents' happiness depends greatly upon their children. This gives children and parents alike strong reasons to fulfill their duties faithfully.

div.title: Verses 2 and 3 — The soul's real needs
div.p: A righteous person may be poor, but the Lord will not let that person lack what is necessary for spiritual life.

div.title: Verse 4 — Diligence in the Lord's service
div.p: People who are fervent in spirit, serving the Lord are likely to become rich in faith and good works.

div.title: Verse 5 — Use opportunities wisely
div.p: Those who waste their opportunities deserve rebuke, for they are neglecting chances to prepare both for this life and the life to come.

div.title: Verse 6 — True blessing
div.p: The blessings resting upon faithful people are not empty appearances: they are real blessings.

div.title: Verse 7 — The difference that outlasts death
div.p: Both righteous and wicked people must die, but their souls face vastly different conditions.

div.title: Verse 8 — Wisdom put into practice
div.p: A person who is wise in heart acts upon the knowledge received.

div.title: Verse 9 — The exposure of deceit
div.p: People who disguise their intentions and continually evade the truth will eventually be found out.

div.title: Verse 10 — Craftiness does not excuse sin
div.p: Cleverness and cunning cannot make wrongdoing innocent.

div.title: Verse 11 — Words that bring life
div.p: A good person speaks to teach, encourage and correct others.

div.title: Verse 12 — Love maintains peace
div.p: Where hatred rules, every small event produces quarrels. By patiently bearing with one another, we preserve peace and harmony.

div.title: Verse 13 — Foolishness invites correction
div.p: Those who persist foolishly in wicked ways are preparing their own punishment.

div.title: Verse 14 — Store up useful knowledge
div.p: We should treasure all knowledge that may be useful, so it will be ready when we need it. We gain this wisdom through reading, listening to God's word, meditation, prayer and faith in Christ, whom God makes wisdom for us.

div.title: Verse 15 — The mistaken confidence of rich and poor
div.p: Both rich and poor people may misunderstand their material circumstances. Wealth can expose people to many dangers. Someone with little may nevertheless live comfortably with contentment, a good conscience and faith.

div.title: Verse 16 — Work that leads to life
div.p: A righteous person may own nothing beyond what hard work produces. Yet that labor leads to life.

div.title: Verse 17 — Receive correction
div.p: A traveler who has lost the way and refuses directions toward the right road will remain lost.

div.title: Verse 18 — Nothing can be hidden from God
div.p: It is especially foolish to imagine anything can be concealed from God. Malice is no less evil.

div.title: Verse 19 — Restrain excessive speech
div.p: Those who speak too much often say many things they should not. Restraining our words is wisdom and helps preserve our peace.

div.title: Verses 20 and 21 — The words of the righteous
div.p: The speech of the righteous is sincere, free from the impurities of deceit and evil design. Godly conversation becomes spiritual nourishment for people in need. Foolish people perish because they lack heart or thoughtful understanding, as the Hebrew expression indicates.

div.title: Verse 22 — Wealth without sorrow
div.p: The truly desirable kind of wealth brings neither anguish in enjoying it, despair when it is lost, nor guilt through misuse. What comes from God's love is accompanied by God's grace.

div.title: Verse 23 — Harm is no game
div.p: Only the foolish and wicked take pleasure in harming others or enticing them into sin.

div.title: Verse 24 — The hope of the righteous
div.p: The righteous person's greatest desire for eternal blessings will be fulfilled.

div.title: Verse 25 — The brief prosperity of sinners
div.p: The apparent success of unrepentant sinners resembles a whirlwind: it soon exhausts itself and vanishes.

div.title: Verse 26 — A lazy worker brings distress
div.p: Just as vinegar irritates the teeth and smoke stings the eyes, a lazy person causes frustration and trouble to an employer.

div.title: Verses 27 and 28 — Reverence and lasting hope
div.p: Who desires life? Fear God. He gives his people all the life necessary in this world and eternal life in the next. Their hope is therefore lasting.

div.title: Verse 29 — The believer grows stronger
div.p: Those who trust God increase in faith, and obedience becomes increasingly delightful to them.

div.title: Verse 30 — Earth is not the wicked person's permanent home
div.p: Wicked people might wish to remain on earth among their idols forever, but they cannot. They must die and leave those idols behind.

div.title: Verses 31 and 32 — Speech that benefits others
div.p: A good person speaks with wisdom for other people's benefit. The wicked speak things displeasing to God and offensive to those around them; this is both their sin and their ruin. The righteous are preserved by God's power, and nothing can separate them from God's love in Christ Jesus.

div.title: Verse 1 — Honest measures
div.p: People may treat false weights and measures as a small offense, especially when the practice is widespread, but God regards such dishonesty as detestable.

div.title: Verse 2 — The safety of humility
div.p: The humble enjoy greater security, peace and ease of mind than the proud. Wisdom belongs with humility.

div.title: Verse 3 — Integrity guides life
div.p: An honest person's principles are settled, so the right path is clear.

div.title: Verse 4 — Money cannot save us from death
div.p: Wealth offers no help when the day of death arrives.

div.title: Verses 5 and 6 — Sin destroys its own followers
div.p: Wicked ways are dangerous. Sin eventually becomes its own punishment.

div.title: Verse 7 — What death removes
div.p: When a godly person dies, all fears vanish. When an ungodly person dies, all false hopes vanish.

div.title: Verse 8 — Providence preserves the upright
div.p: The righteous are often wonderfully kept from danger, while the wicked fall into the trouble they escaped.

div.title: Verse 9 — The dangers of hypocritical speech
div.p: Hypocrites mislead others into wrongdoing by using clever objections to God's word.

div.title: Verses 10 and 11 — A community relieved of wickedness
div.p: A nation prospers when wicked people lose their power to injure it.

div.title: Verse 12 — Judge character, not success
div.p: A person of understanding does not judge someone else's worth merely by outward prosperity.

div.title: Verse 13 — Keep confidences faithfully
div.p: A trustworthy person keeps confidential matters private, unless God's honor or the genuine good of society requires disclosure.

div.title: Verse 14 — The value of counsel
div.p: Consulting others often brings important advantages. We should not assume our judgment needs no advice.

div.title: Verse 15 — Consider the cost of guaranteeing debts
div.p: Do not endanger your family's welfare, your peace of mind or your ability to pay rightful debts by undertaking obligations you cannot meet. But remember the extraordinary grace of Jesus Christ, who became Surety for his enemies.

div.title: Verse 16 — The honor of a wise woman
div.p: A godly, prudent woman preserves respect and esteem as firmly as strong people protect their wealth.

div.title: Verse 17 — Cruelty harms the cruel
div.p: A cruel, ill-tempered person causes suffering to those who ought to be treated as his own flesh, and punishes himself through that cruelty.

div.title: Verse 18 — Doing good has a sure reward
div.p: Those who make doing good their work have a reward as certain as God's eternal truth.

div.title: Verse 19 — Holiness is happiness
div.p: True holiness brings true happiness. The more fiercely someone pursues sin, the faster destruction approaches.

div.title: Verse 20 — God hates double dealing
div.p: Nothing is more offensive to God than hypocrisy and deceit. He delights in people whose intentions and conduct are sincere.

div.title: Verse 21 — A crowd cannot protect sinners
div.p: Joining together with others to commit sin does not make anyone safe from judgment.

div.title: Verse 22 — Beauty without discretion
div.p: Physical beauty is misused when separated from modesty and sound judgment. The same applies to other bodily advantages.

div.title: Verse 23 — Evil desires recoil upon their owner
div.p: Wicked people desire harm for others, but their schemes return upon themselves.

div.title: Verse 24 — Misers can lose what they withhold
div.p: People may become poor by refusing to pay just debts, help the poor or meet necessary expenses. Even careful hoarding can come to nothing whenever God so appoints.

div.title: Verse 25 — Generosity and God's provision
div.p: In spiritual and earthly matters, God commonly treats his people according to the measure of generosity they show their neighbors.

div.title: Verse 26 — Do not hoard God's gifts
div.p: We must not store up the blessings of God's bounty only to advance our own interests.

div.title: Verse 27 — Seek good, not harm
div.p: Seeking harm is contrasted with seeking good. Those who refuse to do good may be doing harm even to themselves.

div.title: Verse 28 — The living Vine
div.p: A believer is a branch of the living Vine, Christ. Those rooted only in worldly wealth will wither, but people grafted into Christ will bear fruit.

div.title: Verse 29 — Troubling your household
div.p: Someone who brings suffering upon self and family through wickedness or carelessness will lose the ability to hold and enjoy possessions—just as no one can grasp the wind or be satisfied by it.

div.title: Verse 30 — Righteousness nourishes others
div.p: The righteous are like trees of life. The influence of their lives nourishes and supports spiritual life in many others.

div.title: Verse 31 — Seek the blessings Christ purchased
div.p: Even righteous people meet severe correction when they sin on earth. How much more will the wicked receive their deserved judgment! Seek the blessings our Surety purchased through his suffering and death, imitate his example and keep his commands.

div.title: Verse 1 — Love instruction
div.p: People who possess God's grace welcome instruction and correction. Those who suppress conviction behave like unreasoning animals.

div.title: Verse 2 — Disguised evil remains evil
div.p: Someone who conceals selfish and corrupt plans under the outward appearance of religion or friendship will be condemned.

div.title: Verse 3 — An enduring foundation
div.p: People may rise through dishonest methods, but they cannot become secure through them. Those who are rooted in Christ by faith are firmly established.

div.title: Verse 4 — A wife who brings honor
div.p: A godly and prudent wife who manages her household well, performs her duties conscientiously and patiently endures hardship brings honor and comfort to her husband. A wife who does the opposite causes him distress and drains his strength.

div.title: Verse 5 — God knows our thoughts
div.p: Thoughts are not beyond moral accountability. God knows them, and they are therefore subject to his commands. Scheming and deceit bring shame.

div.title: Verse 6 — Words can wound or help
div.p: Wicked people use their words to injure neighbors. Yet even one good word can sometimes accomplish a valuable work.

div.title: Verse 7 — The households of the righteous
div.p: God's blessing often continues within the families of godly people even when the wicked are brought down.

div.title: Verse 8 — Wisdom in suffering disgrace
div.p: The apostles displayed wisdom by rejoicing to suffer dishonor for Christ's name.

div.title: Verse 9 — Humble sufficiency
div.p: Someone who works for daily bread without servants is happier than a person boasting of noble ancestry or fine clothing while lacking life's necessities.

div.title: Verse 10 — Kindness to animals
div.p: A godly person does not impose unnecessary pain even on an animal. Wicked people may describe as merciful treatment that they themselves could not bear for a single day.

div.title: Verse 11 — Attend to honest work
div.p: It is wise to work diligently at an honest occupation. Neglecting ordinary responsibilities is folly; God's grace teaches us to despise nothing except sin.

div.title: Verse 12 — Do not envy unlawful gains
div.p: When wicked people see others prospering through sin, they may wish to imitate them. But God's grace rooted in the righteous heart produces different desires and aims.

div.title: Verse 13 — The costly misuse of speech
div.p: Many people have paid dearly, even during this life, for sins committed with their lips.

div.title: Verse 14 — Speech that serves others
div.p: People who rightly use their words to instruct and comfort others enjoy acceptance through Jesus Christ and the conscience's encouragement that they have, in some measure, fulfilled their purpose.

div.title: Verse 15 — The fool's own standard
div.p: In Scripture the fool is a wicked person who rejects wisdom from above. The rule of life becomes whatever is right in that person's own eyes.

div.title: Verse 16 — Restrain anger
div.p: A fool becomes angry quickly and displays it recklessly, thereby inviting trouble. We treat ourselves kindly when we overlook insults rather than making the worst of them.

div.title: Verse 17 — Be ruled by truth
div.p: Everyone should regard lying with abhorrence and be guided by honest speech.

div.title: Verse 18 — A healing tongue
div.p: Whispered accusations and unfounded suspicions cut like swords, separating even close friends. But the speech of wise people brings healing.

div.title: Verse 19 — Truth endures
div.p: Truth remains firm and valid even when people dislike hearing it.

div.title: Verse 20 — Peace brings joy
div.p: Deceit and lies bring terror and confusion. Those who seek others' peace and happiness find joy in their own hearts.

div.title: Verse 21 — The security of the righteous
div.p: God has promised protection to those who are genuinely righteous. But people who delight in causing harm will experience plenty of harm themselves.

div.title: Verse 22 — Truthful words and conduct
div.p: Make honesty a matter of conscience in actions as well as words.

div.title: Verse 23 — Folly announces itself
div.p: Foolish people publicly expose the emptiness and folly of their own thinking.

div.title: Verse 24 — Diligence is honorable
div.p: People who avoid honest work and try to survive through tricks and dishonesty reduce themselves to a miserable condition.

div.title: Verse 25 — Encouragement in anxiety
div.p: Worry, fear and sorrow weaken people's strength for duty and courage in suffering. A good word from God, received through faith, restores joy to the heart.

div.title: Verse 26 — Real riches in the Spirit
div.p: Righteous people possess abundance even when they lack worldly wealth: the Spirit's graces and comforts are true riches. Wicked people falsely assure themselves their chosen way is harmless.

div.title: Verse 27 — Use opportunities well
div.p: Lazy people waste the advantages Providence has given and receive no comfort from them. The diligent person's possessions, even if modest, bless that person and the family and are received gratefully as God's answer to prayer.

div.title: Verse 28 — Life on the path
div.p: True religion leads along a straight and clearly marked way of righteousness. Life is found not only at the end of the path but along it, through genuine spiritual comfort.

div.title: Verse 1 — Respect faithful correction
div.p: Children who honor their parents give reason for hope. Little hope remains for those who refuse to listen to people who faithfully correct them.

div.title: Verse 2 — Accountability for speech
div.p: By our words we will be justified or condemned (Matthew 12:37).

div.title: Verse 3 — Guard the tongue
div.p: Thinking before we speak, and refusing to utter evil thoughts, protects the soul from much guilt and grief. Many have ruined themselves through an uncontrolled tongue.

div.title: Verse 4 — Desire without diligence
div.p: Lazy people desire what diligent people gain but refuse the effort needed to obtain it. Their desires remain unsatisfied. This is especially true in spiritual life.

div.title: Verse 5 — Sin makes us repulsive
div.p: Where sin rules, a person becomes detestable. A conscience awakened to sin would lead to self-abhorrence and repentance in dust and ashes.

div.title: Verse 6 — A sincere desire to do right
div.p: The honest determination to do what is right guards a person from disastrous mistakes more effectively than a thousand elaborate distinctions.

div.title: Verse 7 — Poverty and wealth can be appearances
div.p: Some people are poor but spend and trade as though rich; this is sinful and leads toward shame. Others are wealthy but pretend to be poor, showing ingratitude to God and injustice and lack of charity toward others. Many hypocrites lack grace but refuse to see their poverty. Many timid Christians possess great spiritual riches yet believe themselves poor; their doubt, complaint and sorrow make them unnecessarily miserable.

div.title: Verse 8 — Riches invite dangers
div.p: Great wealth can expose its owner to threats and violence from which the poor are often free.

div.title: Verse 9 — Light that endures
div.p: A righteous person's light resembles the sun: clouds or an eclipse may obscure it, but it continues to shine. The Spirit is their light and gives full joy. The wicked person's light is like a lamp lit by human hands, easily extinguished.

div.title: Verse 10 — Pride feeds quarrels
div.p: Disputes between people, families, churches and nations begin and continue through pride. Without pride, disagreements would often be prevented or quickly settled.

div.title: Verse 11 — Dishonest wealth wastes away
div.p: Wealth obtained through fraud or sin carries a hidden curse and soon disappears.

div.title: Verse 12 — Hope delayed and fulfilled
div.p: Long delays in receiving something eagerly expected cause pain; receiving it brings delight. Henry says spiritual blessings are chiefly in view here.

div.title: Verse 13 — Reverence for God's word
div.p: Those who fear God and honor his word escape destruction and receive the reward of reverent obedience.

div.title: Verse 14 — Wisdom is a fountain
div.p: The principles that guide a wise person's life become a fountain of life and happiness.

div.title: Verse 15 — Sin is harsh slavery
div.p: The sinner's path harms other people and the sinner too. Serving sin is slavery, and the road toward hell is strewn with the thorns and thistles of the curse.

div.title: Verse 16 — Do not speak beyond knowledge
div.p: It is foolish to speak confidently on subjects we know nothing about or to undertake work we are wholly unqualified to perform.

div.title: Verse 17 — Faithful messengers bring healing
div.p: Those who are unfaithful to Christ and other people's souls bring and suffer harm. Faithful messengers find that sound words heal both themselves and those who hear them.

div.title: Verse 18 — Despising instruction leads down
div.p: Those who refuse to be taught will eventually be humbled.

div.title: Verse 19 — The false pleasure of sin
div.p: Human beings long intensely for happiness. But people unwilling to abandon their sins should not expect any sweetness that can truly satisfy their souls.

div.title: Verse 20 — Choose companions wisely
div.p: Bad company brings multitudes to ruin. Those who make themselves wicked will be destroyed.

div.title: Verse 21 — God's justice overtakes sinners
div.p: When God pursues sinners in judgment, he will overtake them. He will also reward the righteous.

div.title: Verse 22 — The best provision for children
div.p: A servant of God who does not live in anxiety over becoming wealthy is actually following the best way to provide for children.

div.title: Verse 23 — Industry and discernment
div.p: Poor people who work hard may prosper modestly, while those with great resources often become poor through foolish management.

div.title: Verse 24 — Loving discipline
div.p: Parents who indulgently allow sinful habits to grow strong act as though they hated their children. Such habits bring sorrow now and may bring misery hereafter.

div.title: Verse 25 — What truly satisfies
div.p: Wicked people find that even their bodily appetites continually demand more. The righteous feed their souls on God's word and appointed ordinances, finding satisfaction in gospel promises and Jesus Christ, the Bread of Life.

div.title: Verse 1 — A household built or destroyed
div.p: A woman who has no fear of God and is willful, wasteful and given to ease can ruin her own household as surely as if she pulled down its walls.

div.title: Verse 2 — Reverence or contempt
div.p: Here grace and sin show their true character. Whoever despises God's commands and promises also despises God's power and mercy.

div.title: Verse 3 — Uproot pride
div.p: Pride grows from bitterness rooted in the heart. We must pull out the root, not merely cut off one visible branch. Wise and prudent words can help people escape difficulties.

div.title: Verse 4 — Useful work involves some inconvenience
div.p: No real advantage is obtained without some difficulty or inconvenience—often something small that nevertheless frightens lazy people.

div.title: Verse 5 — Witness truthfully
div.p: A conscientious witness will never knowingly describe events differently from what he or she actually knows.

div.title: Verse 6 — Humility receives wisdom
div.p: A scoffer treats God's truth with contempt. Someone conscious of ignorance and unworthiness approaches Scripture humbly.

div.title: Verse 7 — Recognize unholy conversation
div.p: A person's speech can reveal wickedness when no evidence of reverence for God can be found in it.

div.title: Verse 8 — Know the road and its destination
div.p: We are travelers. Our concern is not to stare at extraordinary sights, but to learn the rules for our journey and the destination toward which we walk. The wicked person deceives himself and continues in error.

div.title: Verse 9 — Do not mock sin or atonement
div.p: Careless people treat sin as something trivial, rather than something to grieve over. Fools mock the sin offering, and those who treat sin lightly also treat Christ lightly.

div.title: Verse 10 — Hidden pain and hidden peace
div.p: We do not know what guilt or consuming passions torment an apparently prosperous sinner. Nor does the world understand a sincere Christian's inward peace, even amid poverty and sickness.

div.title: Verse 11 — What upholds a household
div.p: Sin has ruined many important families, while righteousness often strengthens and raises households of humble standing.

div.title: Verse 12 — Self-deception leads to destruction
div.p: Careless, worldly and sensual paths can seem right to those traveling them. Those who deceive themselves may destroy themselves. The joy promised by fleshly pleasure is vain.

div.title: Verse 14 — The dread of returning to sin
div.p: Of all sinners, people who have knowingly turned away from their former faith can experience especially terrible fear when reflecting upon their course.

div.title: Verse 15 — Do not believe everything
div.p: Readiness to believe anyone's claims can be deeply harmful; Henry recalls how the world first fell through misplaced trust. Spiritually wise people rely on the Savior alone for acceptance and guard themselves through God's word.

div.title: Verse 16 — Holy fear protects
div.p: Reverent fear of God guards us against everything unholy.

div.title: Verse 17 — Anger and revenge
div.p: Someone who loses their temper quickly deserves both rebuke and pity. Deliberate revengefulness is still more hateful.

div.title: Verse 18 — Wisdom brings honor
div.p: Sin brings shame upon sinners; wisdom brings honor to the wise.

div.title: Verse 19 — Goodness recognized even by enemies
div.p: Even wicked people sometimes have to acknowledge the excellence of God's faithful servants.

div.title: Verse 20 — Friendship beyond self-interest
div.p: Worldly friendship often depends on personal advantage. How good it is to have God as our Friend: he will never abandon us.

div.title: Verse 21 — Do not despise poverty
div.p: Looking down on someone because of occupation, clothing or outward appearance is sinful.

div.title: Verse 22 — Plan to do good
div.p: Those who not only do good but actively devise ways of doing good wisely pursue their own best interests.

div.title: Verse 23 — Real work versus empty talk
div.p: Both intellectual and manual labor can produce good results. But religion consisting only of loud words without action will achieve nothing.

div.title: Verse 24 — Use wealth for good
div.p: The possessions of wise and godly people should enlarge their opportunities to be useful to others.

div.title: Verse 25 — Courageous truthful testimony
div.p: An upright witness will risk even the displeasure of powerful people rather than conceal the truth.

div.title: Verses 26 and 27 — Reverent confidence and the fountain of life
div.p: Those who fear the Lord so as to obey and serve him have a solid basis for confidence and will be kept in his care. Seek this fountain of life and escape death's traps.

div.title: Verse 28 — Seek the growth of Christ's kingdom
div.p: Everyone who desires the good of Christ's kingdom should do what they can to bring more people into his church.

div.title: Verse 29 — Patience resembles Christ
div.p: A gentle and patient person is learning from Christ, who is Wisdom. Uncontrolled passion reveals folly.

div.title: Verse 30 — A peaceful heart helps health
div.p: Integrity, contentment and kindness contribute toward the well-being of the body.

div.title: Verse 31 — The poor bear the Creator's image
div.p: To oppress poor people is to insult their Creator.

div.title: Verse 32 — Death and a reliable hope
div.p: Wicked people die under sin's guilt and power, as though life were forcibly taken from them. Godly people may suffer and fear death to some degree, but they possess God's true promise and a blessed hope.

div.title: Verse 33 — Wisdom in the heart
div.p: Wisdom dwells within the heart and therefore governs affections, attitudes and temper.

div.title: Verse 34 — Godliness benefits society
div.p: True devotion and holiness promote industry, sobriety and honesty.

div.title: Verse 35 — The King values humble service
div.p: The great King who rules heaven and earth rewards faithful servants who honor his gospel by fulfilling duties appropriate to their place. He does not despise even the lowest service.

div.title: Verse 1 — Gentle words calm anger
div.p: A just cause is better defended with gentleness than with a hot temper. Nothing provokes anger more quickly than harsh words.

div.title: Verse 2 — Share knowledge for others' benefit
div.p: Those who possess knowledge ought to use it wisely for the good of other people.

div.title: Verse 3 — Nothing is hidden from God
div.p: God sees every secret sin, secret act of service and secret sorrow. His knowledge comforts the faithful and warns the ungodly.

div.title: Verse 4 — The healing power of speech
div.p: Kind and truthful speech brings healing to wounded consciences by comfort, convinces spiritually sick souls of their need, and reconciles people who have quarreled.

div.title: Verse 5 — Do not let others walk toward ruin
div.p: When people reject instruction, we should continue to correct them faithfully rather than allow them to proceed undisturbed toward destruction.

div.title: Verse 6 — Worldly wealth can multiply fears
div.p: The riches of those devoted to the world may increase their suspicion, stir their passions and make the fear of death still more distressing.

div.title: Verse 7 — Spread good knowledge
div.p: We use knowledge well when we share it with others. Foolish people's hearts have little that is good to offer.

div.title: Verses 8 and 9 — Christ's atonement and sincere obedience
div.p: The wicked try to place other things in the place of Christ's atonement or of holy obedience. The grace to pray rightly is God's gift and the Spirit's work, which is pleasing to him.

div.title: Verse 10 — Do not reject reproof
div.p: People who hate correction and refuse to part with their sins will perish in them.

div.title: Verse 11 — Even human thoughts are open
div.p: Nothing can be hidden from God—not even the deepest thoughts of the heart.

div.title: Verse 12 — The scorner avoids self-examination
div.p: Someone who mocks holiness cannot endure seriously examining the condition of the heart.

div.title: Verse 13 — The misery of a gloomy spirit
div.p: A continually ungrateful, impatient and darkened spirit—often nourished by pride and excessive attachment to worldly things—makes life difficult for oneself and others.

div.title: Verse 14 — Continue growing in wisdom
div.p: Wise people seek further wisdom, growing in grace and knowledge of Christ. Worldly minds rest content while flattering themselves.

div.title: Verse 15 — Comfort the suffering and rejoice reverently
div.p: People weighed down by suffering and sorrow deserve pity, prayer and comfort. Others serve God joyfully and find that joy strengthens obedience, yet they should still rejoice with reverence.

div.title: Verses 16 and 17 — Enough with the Lord
div.p: God's people may possess enough while worldly observers think they have almost nothing. The Lord's presence is better than the worries, temptations and troubles that accompany ungodly wealth.

div.title: Verse 18 — Be slow to anger
div.p: Patient people not only avoid starting quarrels, but can also calm conflicts once they begin.

div.title: Verse 19 — Laziness invents obstacles
div.p: Those unwilling to work imagine excessive hardship or danger in their duties. Many also remain uncertain about their spiritual condition because they keep neglecting some known duty.

div.title: Verse 20 — Honor aging parents
div.p: Contempt for an elderly father or mother reveals a person's own foolishness.

div.title: Verse 21 — Wisdom shapes the whole life
div.p: Truly wise people seek to keep thoughts, words and actions orderly, sincere and holy.

div.title: Verse 22 — Think before acting
div.p: People unwilling to take time and effort to consult and deliberate are unlikely to accomplish their plans.

div.title: Verse 23 — Speak appropriately
div.p: Wisdom is needed to fit our words to the occasion.

div.title: Verse 24 — Set the heart on heaven
div.p: A godly person sets affections upon the things above, and life's path leads toward them.

div.title: Verse 25 — God opposes pride and supports the afflicted
div.p: Pride has destroyed multitudes, but God upholds those who are suffering.

div.title: Verse 26 — God knows sinful thoughts
div.p: Wicked thoughts offend the Lord, who knows what is within the heart.

div.title: Verse 27 — Greed troubles the family
div.p: Covetous people deprive their own households of peace and enjoyment. Greed often entices them into reckless projects that end in ruin.

div.title: Verse 28 — Wisdom governs speech
div.p: A godly person's wise control over the tongue is evidence of genuine wisdom.

div.title: Verse 29 — Rebellion creates distance
div.p: God withdraws his favor from people who openly defy him.

div.title: Verse 30 — The joyful news of salvation
div.p: How wonderful it is for a humbled soul to hear the good news of salvation through the Lord Jesus Christ!

div.title: Verse 31 — A kind rebuke is a gift
div.p: Faithful and friendly correction supports spiritual life and leads toward eternal life.

div.title: Verse 32 — Do not sacrifice the soul for the body
div.p: Sinners undervalue their own souls and therefore prefer bodily pleasure even when it harms the soul.

div.title: Verse 33 — Reverence, Scripture and grace
div.p: The fear of God moves us to search the Scriptures reverently and follow the Holy Spirit's leading. As we humbly depend on God's grace, we are exalted through Christ's righteousness.

div.title: Verse 1 — God prepares the heart
div.p: Only God's renewing grace prepares the heart for every good work. By ourselves, we lack even the ability to think or speak what is truly wise and good.

div.title: Verse 2 — Our self-judgment is biased
div.p: Ignorance, pride and self-flattery make us partial judges of our own conduct.

div.title: Verse 3 — Entrust your cares to God
div.p: Lay the burden of your concerns upon God, leaving it there in faith and dependence on him.

div.title: Verse 4 — God overrules the wicked
div.p: God uses the wicked to execute righteous vengeance upon one another, and he will be glorified by their destruction at last.

div.title: Verse 5 — Pride cannot escape judgment
div.p: Even when sinners join forces to strengthen themselves, they cannot escape God's judgment.

div.title: Verse 6 — Mercy and truth in Christ
div.p: Through God's mercy and truth revealed in Jesus Christ, believers' sins are removed and sin's power is broken.

div.title: Verse 7 — God can reconcile enemies
div.p: The One who holds every human heart in his hand can move even someone's enemies to make peace.

div.title: Verse 8 — Honest means are better
div.p: A small possession honestly acquired is more useful and blessed than a large fortune obtained by wrongdoing.

div.title: Verse 9 — The Lord directs our steps
div.p: If we make God's glory our goal and his will our rule, he will guide our steps by his Spirit and grace.

p.hi: Kings and judges on earth must be just and govern in the fear of God.

div.title: Verse 11 — Justice in commerce
div.p: Honesty and justice in dealings between people are appointed by God.

div.title: Verse 12 — A ruler's true security
div.p: A ruler who exercises authority rightly finds justice to be the surest protection of that office.

div.title: Verse 13 — Wise speech in positions of trust
div.p: Those appointed to authority should know how to speak what is appropriate and useful.

div.title: Verses 14 and 15 — Value God's favor above royal favor
div.p: How foolish it is to seek the favor of an earthly ruler by forfeiting the favor of God.

div.title: Verse 16 — The worth of wisdom
div.p: Only true wisdom provides deep joy and lasting satisfaction of spirit.

div.title: Verse 17 — Keep far from evil
div.p: A sincerely godly person avoids even the appearance of wrongdoing. Blessed are those who walk in Christ and follow his Spirit.

div.title: Verse 18 — Pride precedes judgment
div.p: When people defy God's judgments and think themselves beyond their reach, punishment may be close. Rather than fearing other people's pride, fear pride within your own heart.

div.title: Verse 19 — Humility before God
div.p: Humility may be despised by the world, but it is infinitely better than pride that turns God into an enemy. Those who understand his word will find what is good.

div.title: Verse 21 — True wisdom lives within
div.p: Someone whose wisdom has taken root in the heart is more genuinely prudent than people who possess dazzling natural talents alone.

div.title: Verse 22 — Wisdom refreshes others
div.p: A wise person is to friends and neighbors like water upon thirsty ground.

div.title: Verse 23 — Know yourself to speak well
div.p: A wise person's understanding of the heart helps that person discover what should be said to others.

div.title: Verse 24 — God's word heals
div.p: The word of God is a remedy for the diseases that weaken the soul.

div.title: Verse 25 — Do not deceive your soul
div.p: The warning calls everyone to take care against self-deception regarding spiritual condition and salvation.

div.title: Verse 26 — Work for eternal food
div.p: We must seek the food that endures to everlasting life rather than laboring only for what perishes.

div.title: Verses 27 and 28 — The labor of doing wrong
div.p: Ungodly people often work harder to cause harm than would be needed to do good. Those who spread malicious whispers separate close friends—an especially hateful yet common evil.

div.title: Verses 29 and 30 — Violence blinds its servants
div.p: Some people work as much harm as they can through force and violence, while refusing to recognize where their actions lead.

div.title: Verse 31 — Let old age be honorable
div.p: Older people especially should be found walking in the way of faith and obedience.

div.title: Verse 32 — Self-control exceeds military strength
div.p: Governing our own passions requires steadier and more demanding discipline than winning a victory over a human enemy.

div.title: Verse 33 — Submit to Providence
div.p: Whatever God appoints in the matters we have entrusted to him, we should receive as his wise determination. Blessed are those who submit to his will, knowing he understands what is truly good for them.

div.title: Verse 1 — Peace at home
div.p: Love and peace within a household are essential to the comfort and happiness of human life.

div.title: Verse 2 — Wisdom is greater than birth
div.p: A wise servant can be more deserving of honor and family affection than a son who lives in wickedness.

div.title: Verse 3 — Trials expose the heart
div.p: God tests our hearts through suffering, often revealing sins that still remain even within a believer.

div.title: Verse 4 — The danger of flattery
div.p: People living in sin often welcome flatterers, especially false teachers who reinforce them in wrongdoing.

div.title: Verse 5 — Do not mock the poor
div.p: Mocking poverty shows contempt for God's providence and his commands.

div.title: Verse 6 — The value of faithful parents
div.p: It is an honor and blessing for grown children to continue enjoying the presence and guidance of wise, godly parents.

div.title: Verse 7 — Good speech needs a good life
div.p: In Proverbs, a fool means a wicked person. Excellent words do not fit such a person, because conduct contradicts speech.

div.title: Verse 8 — How gifts rule covetous hearts
div.p: People who make money their chief desire may do almost anything to acquire it. How much more should the gifts of God influence our hearts toward him!

div.title: Verse 9 — Forgive and overlook offenses
div.p: Peace is preserved by giving the most charitable interpretation possible and not continually recalling every wrong spoken or done against us.

div.title: Verse 10 — The wise receive correction
div.p: A gentle rebuke enters not only the thoughts but the heart of someone who is wise.

div.title: Verse 11 — Rebellion invites judgment
div.p: Satan and his messengers are allowed to confront those who persist stubbornly in evil.

div.title: Verse 12 — Avoid uncontrolled rage
div.p: Guard your own passions carefully, and avoid the company of people whose anger is violent and unrestrained.

div.title: Verse 13 — Do not repay good with evil
div.p: Returning evil for good is devilish conduct and can bring a curse upon one's household.

div.title: Verse 14 — Stop conflict before it begins
div.p: The earliest stage of a quarrel is especially dangerous. Resist it at the first sign; if possible, leave the dispute before it even begins.

div.title: Verse 15 — Judge impartially
div.p: God is offended both when a guilty person is declared innocent and when someone innocent is condemned.

div.title: Verse 16 — Do not neglect true wisdom
div.p: It is absurd for human beings to disregard God's favor and their own true interests.

div.title: Verse 17 — Faithful friendship and Christ
div.p: Changes in wealth or circumstances should not weaken love for friends and relatives. Yet only Christ deserves unreserved confidence. In him this promise of faithful friendship finds its greatest fulfillment.

div.title: Verse 18 — Human guarantees and the divine Surety
div.p: Never endanger your family by rash financial promises. But Christ's decision to become Surety for humanity was a glorious act of divine wisdom: he was fully able to pay the debt.

div.title: Verse 19 — Avoid anger and vain display
div.p: Those seeking a peaceful conscience should avoid needless provocations to anger. Living above one's means in order to impress others is a road toward ruin.

div.title: Verse 20 — Schemes and uncontrolled speech
div.p: Evil plans bring no real advantage. Many people have suffered severely because they could not restrain their tongues.

div.title: Verse 21 — Sorrow from a foolish child
div.p: The wickedness and folly of a child cause profound grief to even wise and godly parents.

div.title: Verse 22 — The mercy of cheerfulness
div.p: It is God's kindness that he permits us to rejoice, gives reasons for joy, and through his grace can make our hearts capable of enjoying it.

div.title: Verse 23 — Bribes reveal guilt
div.p: The wicked can be willing to surrender even money they dearly love in order to escape the consequences of their crimes.

div.title: Verse 24 — Keep wisdom in view
div.p: Prudent people continually keep God's word before them. Foolish people cannot settle their thoughts or persevere steadily in a good purpose.

div.title: Verse 25 — Children can wound both parents
div.p: Wicked children despise a father's rightful authority and a mother's tenderness.

div.title: Verse 26 — Do not punish duty
div.p: It is seriously wrong to blame or penalize someone for doing what duty requires.

div.title: Verses 27 and 28 — Temperance in speech
div.p: Wise people show themselves through calmness of spirit and control over the tongue. When they speak, they choose words that serve a purpose. God alone sees every heart perfectly and cannot be misled by appearances.

div.title: Verse 1 — Seek every means of spiritual growth
div.p: Those who want knowledge and grace should make use of every appropriate way of growing in them.

div.title: Verse 2 — Knowledge is not for display
div.p: People who study or profess religion only to have something impressive to show others have missed its true purpose.

div.title: Verse 3 — Shame follows sin
div.p: As soon as sin entered the world, shame followed it.

div.title: Verse 4 — The spring of wisdom
div.p: Wisdom stored in a believer's heart becomes a continual spring of wise words.

div.title: Verse 5 — Judge the cause, not the person
div.p: What matters is the justice of a case, not the social standing or identity of the person involved.

div.title: Verses 6 and 7 — The harm of uncontrolled speech
div.p: Wicked people cause extraordinary harm to themselves through words they refuse to govern.

div.title: Verse 8 — Do not sow suspicion
div.p: Spreading quarrels and whispers is contemptible. Even small beginnings of jealousy may produce dreadful consequences.

div.title: Verse 9 — Neglecting duty is also dangerous
